part: Cat5e patch lead, STRANDED, ~2m, UTP or STP
description: Umbilical cable, module to instrument
notes: *** GAUGE IS OPEN AND THREE DERIVATIONS ASSUME 24 AWG. *** 0005:91 computes a ~0.34 ohm round trip, breath-sense-link.md:100 a 0.168 ohm return term, and 0003:315 a whole signal-drop table - all at 24 AWG, which this row does not specify. A stranded Cat5e PATCH lead is commonly 26 or 28 AWG, at 1.6x to 2.6x the resistance. WHAT DECIDES IT: buy the lead, read the jacket print, or measure end-to-end DC resistance at E6. Note the trap - the well-argued STRANDED requirement below is exactly what makes a thinner gauge likely, and nobody connected the two. STRANDED not solid-core: solid core work-hardens and fractures under constant flexing, which is this cable's whole life. A SHIELD BUYS NOTHING HERE: neither etherCON terminates it (their G tabs are on no net, ADR 0027 'What it is not'), so UTP and STP serve alike. It is a CONSUMABLE - keep spares and replace at the first intermittency

part: Ettinger 5.52.015, plain spacer M2.5 (bore 2.6, L 1.5), faced to 1.3
description: Between the key plate's underside and the key board's top face on each column: it alone sets the key board's depth
notes: ONE PER COLUMN: count = the sum of drc.echo 'key-board mounts' over both boards. It is the whole gap between the plate and the board, the switches' housing below the plate, so the board is pressed against the housings without the column screw pulling it into the plate (ADR 0020 Amendments 6 and 7). It sets the key boards' depth, switch.pcb_below_seat: drc.echo 'key-board mount sets the board depth', and 'key-board depth at the hardware's tolerance limits'. It bears on the board's top copper, so the PCB keeps copper out from under it (grown by hardware.kb_mount_float); kept off the switch cutouts by drc.echo 'key-board spacers clear of the switch cutouts'. Buy with MECH-MB-SPACER, the same part faced alike. MATERIAL: Ettinger's catalogue lists the 5.52 series as stainless steel, its article sheet for 5.52.023 as nickel-plated brass - either serves; confirm at order. DRAWINGS: datasheets/mechanical/ETTINGER-CATALOG-2024-P79-DISTANZHUELSEN-MESSING.html (the series); datasheets/mechanical/ETTINGER-005.52.015-SPACER-2.6x4.5x1.5-BRASS-NI.pdf (this part). part: PEM FHL-M2.5-10ZI self-clinching flush-head stud, low-displacement head, zinc-plated steel
description: Pressed into the bottom plate from its underside at every one of the main board's mounts, head flush; carries the spacer, the main board, and a column's standoff or an end mount's nut
notes: ONE PER MOUNT ON THE BOTTOM PLATE. COUNT: mechanical/drc.echo 'main board mounts on the bottom plate' (columns and end mounts). PRESSED INTO THE PLATE BY THE PLATE VENDOR (or on a press): hole hardware.stud_hole, NOT DEBURRED, stud inserted from the punch side, squeezed flush on a flat parallel anvil - for sheet this thin, PEM's countersunk anvil 8003302 with punch 975200997 [datasheets/mechanical/PEM-FH-SELF-CLINCHING-STUDS.pdf p.FH-18, FH-20]. Never hammered. FHL, not FH: FHL holds its data in 1.2 mm aluminium and needs 2.8 from an edge - a thumb switch's cutout, a U-bolt hole and the plate's outline all count (hardware.stud_edge; drc.echo 'bottom-plate studs clear of the plate's edges and cutouts'); rated for aluminium to HRB 80 / HB 150, so 5052 or 6061. Zinc-plated steel, not stainless: PEM's finish guide calls stainless in aluminium a significant galvanic pair and plated steel acceptable [datasheets/mechanical/PEM-TECHSHEET-CHOOSING-A-FASTENER-FINISH.pdf pp.3-4]. LENGTH 10: the plate, spacer and main board and 1.5 d into the column standoff at its shortest (hardware.stud_l; drc.echo 'column: stud thread in the standoff', 'end mounts: stud thread past the nut', 'bottom-plate studs: unthreaded shank ends inside the spacer'). TIGHTEN THE STANDOFF OR NUT ON IT TO NO MORE THAN hardware.stud_torque. IT CARRIES THE PLATES' GROUND (ADR 0025): its clinch bonds the bottom plate, and through the column's standoff and screw the key plate, to the main board's plated PWR_GND pads. DRAWING: datasheets/mechanical/PEM-FHL-M2.5-10ZI-SALES-DRAWING.pdf. US SOURCE: not yet found [UNVERIFIED - ask the plate vendor, who presses them]

part: RTV silicone - ALKOXY (alcohol) neutral cure, electronics-safe
description: Bonds the cassette into the shell - the key plate to the oak top, the bottom plate to the oak bottom - the oak top to the sides at the grooves, and the matrix diffuser

Compliant in shear so the oak's 0.6-0.9mm of cross-grain humidity movement does not fight the aluminium plates. Keep it off both sensor ports (ADR 0003) and out of the column screws' pockets. SERVICE IS BY CUTTING IT (ADR 0025): every joint it makes is one that may have to open, so it is the adhesive there, fresh, and nothing harder is used on them. part: 2-layer PCB - 10HP CV interface, jack board
description: The board behind the panel that carries the jacks and pots
notes: TWO LAYERS, 1.6MM: its only ground is AGND_MOD, arriving on J-B2B-MOD's five ground pins, so it has nothing for a second layer pair to separate (dig-gnd-topology). The metal standoffs' pads here are AGND_MOD. WHERE THE JACKS' BODIES PUT IT, behind the panel (ADR 0023). A PLAIN RECTANGLE, full width, ending just below the bottom jack row (config/module.yaml boards.jack_y0), above SW-POWER's body and the NE8FAV (ADR 0024 point 15). The jacks lie on their sides, pins across the panel. Outline, positions and keep-outs: mechanical/module/export/pcb-geometry.echo. SW-POWER is panel-mounted and wired

part: 2-layer PCB - 10HP CV interface, iso board
description: The board behind the main board that carries the instrument's isolated supply (U-ISO and its filter)
notes: TWO LAYERS, 1.6MM: it carries U-ISO, L-ISO-IN, L-CM-ISO, C2 (C-ISO-BULK), C-ISO-IN, C-ISO-Y and C-ISO-OUT and nothing analog - the power-entry circuit's page iso (hardware/module/power-entry). THE OWNER, 2026-10-03: '3 boards for module is correct' (ADR 0023 point 2, amended). PARALLEL TO THE MAIN BOARD, BEHIND IT, on the stock spacers uncut (MECH-STANDOFF-ISO); its parts on its REAR face. Its outline is derived (config/module.yaml iso_board; mechanical/module/export/iso-board.dxf): the boards' side edges, above the NE8FAV's tails, a notch for J-PWR-EURO, below the rear trimmers so each stays adjustable from behind. Every standoff pad on this board is on NO net. Keep U-ISO's input nets and its output nets apart by the layout's isolation gap (hardware/boards/module-iso/layout.yaml isolation)

part: M3 female-female hex spacer, METAL, 8mm stock, FACED to length
description: Holds the jack board and the main board apart, above the pots
notes: METAL (owner, 2026-09-30: 'Metal standoffs'). TWO, above the pots (config/module.yaml standoff.at); the main board's two low mounting points are MECH-PANEL-STANDOFF-MOD, since the jack board ends above the toggle's row (ADR 0024 point 15). ITS PADS: AGND_MOD on the jack board (H1, H2), NO NET on the main board - so they add no second ground tie between the boards (dig-gnd-topology). The metal part is not chosen yet: config/module.yaml standoff.* still cites the polyamide Wurth 970080365's datasheet (8.0 +/-0.1, SW 6), and the metal part must meet those or the CAD's leaves change - the module CAD owner decides. FACE EACH ONE to mechanical/module/drc.echo 'standoff length (derived)' from the 8mm bought, and measure it (drc.echo 'standoff faced from stock'): the gap is the NE8FAV's setback less the jack's body and the jack board, and neither board's depth can move to suit (ADR 0024 point 8)

part: M3 female-female hex spacer, METAL, 8mm stock, NOT faced
description: Holds the iso board off the main board's rear face
notes: THE SAME 8mm STOCK SPACER AS MECH-STANDOFF-MOD, USED UNCUT: its length IS the gap between the main board's rear face and the iso board (mechanical/module/drc.echo 'iso board gap'), so the board follows the spacer, not the other way round. TWO, at opposite corners (config/module.yaml iso_board.standoff_at), with J-B2B-ISO soldered through both boards near the third. ITS PADS: NO NET on both boards. Each takes two MECH-STANDOFF-SCREW-MOD, one from the main board's front, one from the iso board's rear

part: M3 female-female hex spacer, METAL, faced to length
description: Holds the main board's two low mounting points off the panel's rear face, on MECH-PANEL-STUD-MOD
notes: TWO, low on the left and right beside the NE8FAV (config/module.yaml panel_standoff.at), below the jack board, which ends above the toggle's row (ADR 0024 point 15). Threaded onto the panel's stud, the main board screwed to its other end from the rear (MECH-STANDOFF-SCREW-MOD). FACE EACH ONE to mechanical/module/drc.echo 'panel standoff length (derived), faced from stock': the gap is the NE8FAV's setback, which the NE8FAV itself fixes, so a spacer that is long or short bends the main board against the connector. Bought at the next stocked length over it (panel_standoff.stock_l, tbd until bought). Metal, as MECH-STANDOFF-MOD; its main-board pad is on no net. The part is not chosen

part: M3 x 8 flush-head self-clinching stud, aluminium
description: The panel end of each MECH-PANEL-STANDOFF-MOD
notes: PEM FHA-M3-8 [ds PEM-FH-SELF-CLINCHING-STUDS.pdf, metric table]: for aluminium sheet of HRB 50 or less, 1.0 min sheet (the panel is 2), a 3.0 hole in the sheet (mechanical/module/export/panel.dxf), 5.6 min hole centre to edge (drc.echo 'panel studs: sheet and edge distance (PEM)'). INSTALLED BY THE PANEL VENDOR, after anodising and before the UV print - the flush D4.6 head SHOWS on the panel's face, inside island C (config/module.yaml panel_standoff.stud_head_d; ADR 0024 point 15). Whether the vendor clinches studs, and whether the print covers the head, is open: the panel vendor's quote

part: M3 pan head screw, DIN 7985 (length: the board plus the spacer's thread)
description: Holds each MECH-STANDOFF-MOD to the jack board (front face) and the main board (rear face), each MECH-STANDOFF-ISO to the main board (front face) and the iso board (rear face), and the main board to each MECH-PANEL-STANDOFF-MOD (rear face)
notes: TWO PER MECH-STANDOFF-MOD AND PER MECH-STANDOFF-ISO, one through each board into the spacer's internal thread, and ONE PER MECH-PANEL-STANDOFF-MOD, through the main board from its rear; the heads are config/module.yaml m3.head_*, and each board keeps parts and copper out of mechanical/module/export/pcb-geometry.echo's 'standoff head' keep-out. Length: 1.6 board plus the spacer's thread depth, read off the spacer bought - for a panel standoff, short of the stud's end inside it (drc.echo 'panel stud in its spacer')

part: M3 x 6 pan head (DIN 7985) + DIN 125 washer
description: Holds the module panel to the case rails
notes: FOUR, at 10HP [ds DOEPFER-A100-CONSTRUCTION-DETAILS-a100m_e.html], through slotted mounting cuts (ADR 0024). The washer is what panel-height-budget assumes; a larger head eats into the clear height. The DIN 7985 head is config/module.yaml m3.head_d, from the banked table

part: Neutrik A-series mounting screw (A-Screw)
description: Holds J-UMBILICAL's flange to the module panel, from the front
notes: The same screw as MECH-ETHERCON-SCREW at the instrument's end, two through the panel into the flange [ds NE8FAV 'Mounting A-Screw']; its length follows the 2 mm panel

part: 16-pin Eurorack power ribbon
description: From the case bus board to J-PWR-EURO
notes: 16-WAY, because J-PWR-EURO is 16-pin for cable commonality - the bus +5 V is not used (ADR 0023 point 3, amended 2026-09-30). Most cases supply one; RED STRIPE = -12V, at J-PWR-EURO's pin 1 and 'down' at the bus board
